g.title: G

Initial-vote evidence. Meaning: Pool has this validator’s first vote and counts the initial votes it has received from other validators. Purpose: Fallback decisions use initial votes as evidence. They do not use fallback votes to establish their own safe conditions.

Safe block fallback test. Meaning: The first vote must differ from NotarVote for B. The formula then tests the observed initial notar and skip stake. Purpose: The evidence must rule out fast finality for a different block. The data and parent checks must also pass.

F01: Check block fallback. When: The validator has a first vote and new initial-vote information. Action: Check the SafeToNotar formula for each related block B. Reason: The validator needs evidence that another block cannot fast-finalize before it adds fallback support for B.

a.xlink:title: The validator needs evidence that another block cannot fast-finalize before it adds fallback support for B.
F01: Check block fallback

g.title: Safe skip fallback test. Meaning: This validator must have sent an initial notar vote. At least 40% observed initial stake must lie outside the largest block group. Purpose: Under the paper’s fault limit, no block can then obtain 80% initial support. Skip fallback can help the network continue.

F02: Check skip fallback. When: The validator has a first vote and new initial-vote information. Action: Check the SafeToSkip formula. Reason: Skip fallback is safe only when no block can get fast finality.

a.xlink:title: Skip fallback is safe only when no block can get fast finality.
F02: Check skip fallback

g.title: Get the fallback block. Meaning: The validator gets block B and checks its identity. Repair supplies missing data. Purpose: The paper requires block data before SafeToNotar. The block data also identifies the parent for the next check.

F03: Block threshold met. When: The first-vote exclusion and one SafeToNotar threshold alternative are true. Action: Get B if its data is missing. Reason: A vote that supports B must meet the paper’s data requirement. The data also identifies the parent.

a.xlink:title: A vote that supports B must meet the paper's data requirement. The data also identifies the parent.
F03: Block threshold met

g.title: SafeToSkip event. Meaning: The initial-vote evidence rules out fast finality for every block in this slot. Purpose: The validator can add skip fallback support if it has not made a final-vote commitment.

F08: Skip threshold met. When: The first vote was a notar vote. S + T - max N(B) is at least 40%. Action: Emit SafeToSkip for the slot. Reason: The initial votes exclude fast finality for every block in the slot.

a.xlink:title: The initial votes exclude fast finality for every block in the slot.
F08: Skip threshold met

g.title: First slot or later slot. Meaning: The validator checks whether B starts the leader window. Purpose: A later block needs extra evidence for its parent in the same window. The first-slot path has a different condition.
F04: Block available. When: The validator has block B. Action: Find its position in the leader window. Reason: The first slot and later slots have different parent requirements.

a.xlink:title: The first slot and later slots have different parent requirements.
F04: Block available

g.title: Wait for the parent certificate. Meaning: The parent of this later-window block needs a notar-fallback certificate or stronger evidence. Purpose: This keeps fallback votes connected to a supported parent chain. The validator waits while that evidence is missing.

F06: Later slot. When: B occupies a later slot in the leader window. Action: Wait for a notar-fallback certificate, or stronger evidence, for its parent. Reason: A child must not receive fallback support without the required evidence for its parent.

a.xlink:title: A child must not receive fallback support without the required evidence for its parent.
F06: Later slot

g.title: SafeToNotar event. Meaning: Pool has enough evidence to permit fallback support for B. The required data and parent conditions hold. Purpose: The event permits a local decision. It does not itself prove 60% fallback support, and it cannot override ItsOver.

F05: First slot. When: B occupies the first slot of the leader window. The earlier checks passed. Action: Emit SafeToNotar for B. Reason: The additional parent-certificate check for a later block in the same window does not apply here.

a.xlink:title: The additional parent-certificate check for a later block in the same window does not apply here.
F05: First slot

g.title: F07: Parent proof available. When: The required parent certificate is available. Action: Emit SafeToNotar for B. Reason: Both the fallback threshold and the parent condition now hold.

a.xlink:title: Both the fallback threshold and the parent condition now hold.
F07: Parent proof available

g.title: Check before the fallback vote. Meaning: The handler first runs trySkipWindow. It then checks ItsOver and whether it already sent this fallback vote. Purpose: These checks preserve the first vote, protect a final-vote commitment, and prevent duplicate new votes.
g.text: If ItsOver is false and the vote is new:

g.title: F09: Consider block fallback. When: The handler receives SafeToNotar for B. Action: Run trySkipWindow. If ItsOver is false and the vote is new, send NotarFallbackVote for B. Reason: The vote helps form a fallback certificate. The ItsOver check protects an earlier final-vote commitment.

a.xlink:title: The vote helps form a fallback certificate. The ItsOver check protects an earlier final-vote commitment.
F09: Consider block\nfallback

g.title: F10: Consider skip fallback. When: The handler receives SafeToSkip for the slot. Action: Run trySkipWindow. If ItsOver is false and the vote is new, send SkipFallbackVote. Reason: The vote helps form a skip certificate. The ItsOver check protects an earlier final-vote commitment.

a.xlink:title: The vote helps form a skip certificate. The ItsOver check protects an earlier final-vote commitment.
F10: Consider skip fallback
